nodes.description: The initiating lesion. Pathogenic UBA5 variants reduce the activity of the UFM1 E1 activating enzyme, by impairing catalysis, ATP binding, or protein stability depending on where the residue sits. This node is the genetic lesion only; the separate enzymatic steps it disrupts are curated as their own nodes below, because the sources measure them separately.

nodes.description: Loss of UFMylation perturbs ER homeostasis and drives an exaggerated unfolded protein response. This is the arm with the most direct human-cell evidence, having been shown both in patient fibroblasts as abnormal ER structure and in patient-derived organoids and engineered cells as an exacerbated UPR.

nodes.description: Single-cell RNA sequencing of patient-derived cortical organoids identified defects in the development of GABAergic interneurons. This is the most disease-proximal inhibitory-side finding available in a human model, and is the node through which this disorder attaches to the conserved excitation-inhibition module.

nodes.description: UBA5 is a non-canonical E1 that carries its catalytic cysteine inside the adenylation domain rather than in a separate domain. It adenylates the UFM1 C-terminal glycine and then forms a thioester bond through Cys250. This node covers those two steps on the enzyme itself, and is kept separate from the handoff to UFC1 because the two are assayed independently and specific variants dissociate them - p.Tyr53Phe leaves E1 activity at 3.4% but transthiolation at 6.8% of wild type.
nodes.id: Impaired UFM1 Adenylation and Thioester Formation

evidence.snippet: In the activation process UBA5 adenylates UFM1 C-terminal Gly and then forms a thioester bond with the UFM1 C-terminus via its active site Cys250
UBA5 is a non-canonical E1 activating enzyme that possesses an adenylation domain but lacks a distinct cysteine domain

molecular_functions: UFM1 adenylation and thioester bond formation at Cys250

nodes.description: Transthiolation - transfer of activated UFM1 from the UBA5 active-site cysteine to the E2 enzyme UFC1. The recurrent hypomorphic p.Ala371Thr allele was characterised specifically at this step, showing attenuated rather than absent transfer, which is what makes it viable in trans with a severe allele.

evidence.snippet: we show that the p.Ala371Thr variant is hypomorphic with attenuated ability to transfer the activated UFM1 to UFC1

molecular_functions: transthiolation transfer of UFM1 to the E2 enzyme UFC1

nodes.description: Accumulation of full-length PINK1 at the outer mitochondrial membrane, the canonical signal for PARKIN recruitment and mitophagy. Curated separately from the structural damage node because it is a distinct measurement (a protein isoform readout, not morphology) and is a cellular response to the damage rather than the damage itself.

nodes.description: Cortical organoids from two individuals, each carrying p.A371T in trans with a nonsense allele, with isogenic controls. The only humanized neuronal model of this disorder.

The cell-level readout of the enzymatic defect - the pool of UFM1-conjugated substrates falls. Curated as its own node rather than merged with the enzymology because it is measured differently (conjugate levels on blot, in an intact animal) and because the zebrafish measurement carries an informative second finding: free, unconjugated Ufm1 falls further than the conjugates do.
